prompt: A homeowner believes a Texas sales agent invented competing offers to pressure her into signing and wants the agent's license disciplined. Which body administers the Texas Real Estate License Act and can act on that license?

options.text: The Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC)
The county district attorney's office
The Department of Savings and Mortgage Lending
The local justice of the peace court

explanation: TREC is the state agency that administers the Texas Real Estate License Act (TRELA, Occupations Code ch. 1101) and its rules. It licenses brokers and sales agents, investigates consumer complaints, and can reprimand, suspend, or revoke a license or assess administrative penalties. Criminal charges and private lawsuits are separate tracks.

distractorExplanations.b: A district attorney prosecutes crimes such as fraud; it does not license agents or discipline a real estate license.
distractorExplanations.c: That department licenses residential mortgage loan originators and thrifts, not real estate brokers or sales agents.
distractorExplanations.d: A justice court hears small civil claims and evictions; it has no power over a person's real estate license.

prompt: A grateful buyer wants to hand sales agent Dana a $1,000 bonus directly after closing. Under TRELA, how may Dana receive compensation for this transaction?

options.text: Directly from the buyer, if she reports the bonus as income
Through her sponsoring broker, who pays her under their agreement
Directly from the buyer, if she tells the listing broker in writing
From the title company as a closing credit payable to her

explanation: TRELA bars a sales agent from accepting compensation for a real estate transaction from anyone other than the broker who sponsors her (or sponsored her when the work was done). The buyer may pay the bonus to Dana's broker, who can then pass it to her under their agreement; a direct payment would be a violation.

distractorExplanations.a: Reporting the bonus for tax purposes does not cure the rule that a sales agent is paid through her sponsoring broker.
distractorExplanations.c: Telling the other broker does not help; the payment must still flow through Dana's own sponsoring broker.
distractorExplanations.d: A title company paying an agent personally is still payment from someone other than her broker and may also be a RESPA kickback.

prompt: TREC revokes the license of the broker who sponsors sales agent Omar while Omar has two active listings. What happens to Omar's license?

options.text: It stays active, and he may finish pending deals under that broker
It stays active for a 30-day grace period while he finds a new broker
It becomes inactive until another active broker sponsors him
It converts to a broker license so he can close the listings himself

explanation: A Texas sales agent may perform brokerage only while sponsored by an active broker. When the sponsoring broker's license is revoked, suspended, or expires, the sponsored agent's license goes inactive. Omar may resume work once a new broker's sponsorship is filed with TREC; the listings belong to the brokerage, not to him.

distractorExplanations.a: Once the sponsor's license is revoked the agent's license is inactive, so he cannot keep working deals under that broker.
distractorExplanations.b: TRELA gives no 30-day grace period; brokerage activity stops until a new active broker sponsors him.
distractorExplanations.d: A sales agent license does not convert on its own; a broker license needs its own experience, education, and exam.

prompt: Sales agent Priya wants to buy a rental house for herself from an owner who is selling without a broker. What do TREC rules require of Priya before she enters into the contract?

options.text: Get the seller's written consent to her acting as an intermediary
Get a TREC waiver, since license holders may not buy from consumers directly
Order an appraisal and give it to the seller before making her offer
Disclose in writing to the seller that she holds a real estate license

explanation: When a license holder buys or sells real estate as a principal (or for a close relative or an entity they control), TREC rules require written disclosure of license status to the other party before entering into a contract. The disclosure warns the owner that they are dealing with a real estate professional and may want their own representation.

distractorExplanations.a: Intermediary status applies when a broker works with both parties for others; Priya is a principal buying for herself.
distractorExplanations.b: License holders may buy and sell property for their own account; TREC requires disclosure, not a waiver.
distractorExplanations.c: No rule requires a buying license holder to hand the seller an appraisal; the required step is disclosing license status.

prompt: Broker Kevin deposits a buyer's $3,000 earnest money check into his brokerage operating account "just until the title company opens on Monday." How is this treated?

options.text: Commingling, because client money sits with brokerage funds
Conversion, because the broker has spent client money on himself
No violation, because the money reaches escrow within a few days
No violation, if the buyer approved the deposit in an email

explanation: Commingling means mixing money that belongs to others with the broker's own or business funds. It is a TRELA violation even for a short time and even if none of the money is spent. Trust money must go to the escrow agent named in the contract or into a properly designated trust account. Conversion is the further step of using the funds.

distractorExplanations.b: Conversion means using client money for the broker's own purposes; nothing has been spent here, so this is mixing, not conversion.
distractorExplanations.c: A short holding period does not excuse placing trust money in an operating account; the deposit itself is the violation.
distractorExplanations.d: A client's informal approval does not authorize mixing trust money with brokerage funds; TREC rules still apply.

prompt: A landlord client asks sales agent Grace to write a custom residential lease with a unique rent-escalation clause and an early-buyout formula. What should Grace do?

options.text: Draft the clauses herself, since license holders may write any lease terms
Refer the client to an attorney to draft them, to avoid practicing law
Use TREC's promulgated residential lease, required for every Texas lease
Draft the clauses and have her sponsoring broker approve them first

explanation: Texas license holders may fill in blanks on promulgated or approved forms, but drafting legal language or advising on its legal effect is the unauthorized practice of law and a ground for TREC discipline. Custom escalation and buyout terms should be drafted by a Texas attorney; Grace can still negotiate the business points for her client.

distractorExplanations.a: License holders may complete forms but may not draft original legal provisions; doing so is unauthorized practice of law.
distractorExplanations.c: TREC does not promulgate a residential lease; widely used residential lease forms come from the Texas REALTORS association.
distractorExplanations.d: Broker review does not cure unauthorized practice of law, since neither license holder may draft legal provisions.

prompt: Which conduct gives TREC grounds to discipline a sales agent's license?

options.text: Charging more than the county maximum commission TREC publishes
Declining to join the local REALTOR association and its MLS
Inducing a buyer to sign with a knowingly false statement
Refusing a seller's request to lower the agreed commission

explanation: TRELA section 1101.652 lists grounds for discipline, including misrepresentation, fraud, dishonesty, failing to disclose known defects, and mishandling trust money. A knowingly false statement used to induce a contract fits squarely. Commission amounts are negotiable, and association or MLS membership is a private choice outside TREC's discipline.

distractorExplanations.a: TREC does not set or publish commission rates; fees are negotiable between broker and client.
distractorExplanations.b: Association and MLS membership are voluntary private matters, so declining them is not a TRELA violation.
distractorExplanations.d: Holding a client to the negotiated commission is lawful; discipline targets dishonesty and rule violations.

prompt: A Dallas property manager negotiates leases and collects rent for several unrelated owners in exchange for a percentage of the rent. Does this activity require a Texas real estate license?

options.text: No, because TRELA licensing covers sales and not leasing
No, because a management fee is not brokerage compensation
Yes, once the manager handles more than ten rental properties
Yes, because leasing for others for a fee is brokerage

explanation: TRELA defines brokerage to include leasing or renting real estate for another person for compensation, and controlling the acceptance or deposit of rent. A third-party manager therefore needs a broker license or must work as a sponsored sales agent. Narrow exemptions exist, such as an on-site apartment manager employed by the owner.

distractorExplanations.a: TRELA's definition of a broker expressly includes leasing and renting real estate for others, not just sales.
distractorExplanations.b: Any fee or percentage paid for leasing services is compensation under TRELA, whatever it is called.
distractorExplanations.c: TRELA sets no property-count threshold; one leasing transaction for another person for a fee requires a license.

prompt: A Texas broker hires an unlicensed assistant. Which task would cross into activity that requires a real estate license?

options.text: Showing a listed home and discussing price and terms with buyers
Placing yard signs and delivering documents at the broker's direction
Scheduling showings and compiling comparable-sales data for an agent
Entering listing data into the MLS and filing transaction paperwork

explanation: Unlicensed assistants may do clerical and support work under the broker's supervision, but they may not perform acts that require a license. Getting this wrong exposes the broker to discipline for aiding unlicensed activity.

distractorExplanations.b: Placing signs and delivering documents are clerical support tasks that unlicensed staff may perform under supervision.
distractorExplanations.c: Scheduling and gathering data for a license holder is administrative work; it does not involve showing or negotiating.
distractorExplanations.d: MLS data entry and paperwork filing are routine office tasks, not acts that require a real estate license.

prompt: A buyer wins a court judgment against a license holder for fraud in a home sale but cannot collect it. What is the Real Estate Recovery Trust Account designed to do?

options.text: Reimburse licensees for commissions that sellers refuse to pay
Pay aggrieved consumers on uncollectable judgments, within caps
Refund earnest money when an escrow title company goes insolvent
Cover licensees' errors-and-omissions claims instead of insurance

explanation: The Recovery Trust Account is funded by license fees and pays actual damages to a person who holds an unsatisfied judgment against a license holder for certain TRELA violations, subject to statutory per-transaction and per-license-holder caps. When the account pays, the license holder's license is revoked until the account is repaid with interest.

distractorExplanations.a: The account protects consumers harmed by license holders; it does not help licensees collect unpaid commissions.
distractorExplanations.c: Title company insolvency is a different risk; the account pays judgments arising from a license holder's misconduct.
distractorExplanations.d: The account is not insurance for license holders; after paying a consumer it pursues the license holder for repayment.

prompt: Texas sales agent Maria meets an unrepresented couple at a coffee shop to talk through their budget and a specific house they want to tour. Under TREC rules, when must she give them the Information About Brokerage Services notice?

options.text: Before they submit an offer on the house
When they sign a written buyer representation agreement
At this first substantive talk about the property
At closing, along with the other required disclosures

explanation: TREC requires license holders to provide the Information About Brokerage Services notice at the first substantive communication with a party about specific real estate. A meeting where buyers discuss their budget and a particular house qualifies, so Maria must deliver it now, before they share more confidential details or choose a type of representation.

distractorExplanations.a: Too late: by offer time the buyers have already discussed specific property and finances, which triggered the notice.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses the IABS notice with the representation agreement; the notice explains the agency options before a buyer chooses one.
distractorExplanations.d: Treats the IABS as a closing document; it is a first-contact disclosure meant to inform the buyer before any dealings.

prompt: Sales agent Tom promotes a new listing in a post on his personal Instagram account. How do TREC advertising rules apply to the post?

options.text: It needs Tom's name and phone, while the broker's name is optional
It is exempt from TREC rules because it is on a personal account
It needs Tom's license number, while broker names apply to signs
It is advertising and must identify Tom's sponsoring broker

explanation: TREC treats social media posts that promote brokerage services as advertising. Every ad must include the broker's licensed name or registered assumed name, and current rules require it to be at least half the size of the largest contact information for a sponsored agent in the ad. Some electronic formats may place required details one click away; check the current rule text.

distractorExplanations.a: Broker identification is mandatory in every ad; leaving the broker's name out is one of the most common advertising violations.
distractorExplanations.b: A personal account does not exempt a post that promotes listings; TREC looks at the content, not the account type.

prompt: Two years after getting licensed, a Texas sales agent is convicted of felony theft. What may TREC do?

options.text: Suspend or revoke the license under its criminal-history guidelines
Nothing, because TREC reviews criminal history before licensing
Refer the matter to the Recovery Trust Account in place of discipline
Wait for the next renewal, since TREC cannot act mid-term

explanation: TRELA and Occupations Code chapter 53 let TREC suspend or revoke a license for a conviction that directly relates to the duties of a license holder. Theft and fraud offenses appear in TREC's criminal-history guidelines because agents handle money and confidential information. License holders must also report convictions to TREC within the deadline its rules set.

distractorExplanations.b: TREC's authority continues after licensing; a conviction during the license term can trigger discipline.
distractorExplanations.c: The Recovery Trust Account pays consumers on unpaid judgments; it is not a substitute for license discipline.
distractorExplanations.d: TREC can open a disciplinary case as soon as it learns of the conviction; it need not wait for renewal.

prompt: Jasmine received her first Texas sales agent license 20 months ago and is preparing for her first renewal. Which education requirement generally applies before that renewal?

options.text: None, because her pre-licensing hours cover the first renewal
Sales Agent Apprentice Education (SAE) courses
Thirty hours of CE each year, with no apprentice courses
None, if she has closed at least ten transactions

explanation: A Texas sales agent's first license runs for two years, and the first renewal requires Sales Agent Apprentice Education (currently 98 classroom hours). After that, each two-year renewal requires continuing education (currently 18 hours, including the TREC Legal Update and contract courses). Confirm current hours with TREC, since the rules change.

distractorExplanations.a: Pre-licensing courses earn the initial license; Texas adds apprentice education before the first renewal.
distractorExplanations.c: Texas uses SAE for the first renewal and then CE per two-year term, not 30 hours a year.
distractorExplanations.d: Transaction volume does not waive TREC education requirements for renewal.

prompt: Which person may negotiate the sale of a Texas house on behalf of the owner without holding a Texas real estate license?

options.text: A Louisiana-licensed broker who travels to Texas to negotiate the deal
The seller's unlicensed cousin, who will receive 1% of the price
A Texas-licensed attorney representing the owner in the sale
A sales agent whose license went inactive, if the buyer agrees

explanation: TRELA exempts certain people from licensing, including an attorney licensed in Texas acting for a client, a person acting under a court order or a duly executed power of attorney, and an on-site apartment manager employed by the owner. Anyone else who negotiates real estate for another person for compensation needs an active Texas license.

distractorExplanations.a: A license from another state does not authorize negotiating in Texas; the out-of-state broker may take a referral fee but not negotiate here.
distractorExplanations.b: Receiving a percentage for negotiating a sale for someone else is brokerage, so the cousin would need a license.
distractorExplanations.d: An inactive license does not authorize brokerage, and a party's consent cannot substitute for an active license.

prompt: A career changer wants to sit for the Texas sales agent exam. How many hours of qualifying pre-licensing education does TREC currently require before she applies?

options.text: 60 hours
90 hours
180 hours
270 hours

explanation: Texas currently requires 180 classroom hours of qualifying education for a sales agent license: six 30-hour courses covering Principles of Real Estate I and II, Law of Agency, Law of Contracts, Promulgated Contract Forms, and Real Estate Finance. Confirm the current course list with TREC before enrolling.

distractorExplanations.a: 60 hours is far below the Texas requirement and equals just two of the six required 30-hour courses.
distractorExplanations.b: 90 hours would be three courses; Texas requires all six 30-hour qualifying courses.
distractorExplanations.d: 270 hours is not the sales agent figure; it overstates the six-course, 180-hour requirement.

prompt: A Texas sales agent candidate passes the national portion of the licensing exam but fails the state portion. What happens next?

options.text: She retakes the state portion, and her national pass stands
She must retake both portions, since they are graded as one exam
She must repeat all qualifying courses before any retest
She may get her license and pass the state portion within a year

explanation: The Texas sales agent exam has a national portion and a state (Texas law) portion, and each is scored separately. A candidate who passes one portion retakes only the portion she failed, within her application period. After repeated failures TREC requires additional education before more attempts, and no license issues until both portions are passed.

distractorExplanations.b: The portions are scored separately, so a passing score on the national portion is kept.
distractorExplanations.c: A single failure does not require repeating qualifying education; extra education applies after repeated failures.
distractorExplanations.d: TREC issues no license until both portions are passed; there is no provisional license while a portion is pending.

prompt: Before TREC will issue a sales agent license, what must an applicant complete as part of the background review?

options.text: A credit check with a minimum score set by TREC
Fingerprinting for a criminal history check
A personal interview with a TREC commissioner
A drug screen arranged by the sponsoring broker

explanation: Texas license applicants must submit fingerprints so TREC can run state and FBI criminal history checks. TREC evaluates any criminal history under its guidelines and Occupations Code chapter 53. TREC does not use credit scores, commissioner interviews, or drug screens as licensing requirements.

distractorExplanations.a: TREC does not set a credit score requirement; it reviews criminal history and honesty, not creditworthiness.
distractorExplanations.c: Commissioners do not interview applicants; the background review is a fingerprint-based record check.
distractorExplanations.d: Drug screening is not a TREC licensing requirement and is not arranged by a sponsoring broker.

prompt: Before paying for pre-licensing courses, a person with a decade-old misdemeanor conviction wants to know whether TREC is likely to license them. What can they request?

options.text: A provisional license that converts after one clean year
A pardon from TREC that clears the conviction record
A waiver of the exam in exchange for extra coursework
A fitness determination from TREC before applying

explanation: TREC offers a fitness determination (formerly called a moral character determination) so a prospective applicant with criminal history or other concerns can learn whether they are likely to qualify before investing in education. TREC reviews the record under its criminal-history guidelines and issues a determination; it does not grant pardons or waive exams.

distractorExplanations.a: TREC has no provisional probationary license for this purpose; the tool is an advance fitness determination.
distractorExplanations.b: Pardons come from the governor; TREC evaluates history but cannot clear a conviction.
distractorExplanations.c: Exam waivers are not offered for criminal-history concerns; every sales agent applicant must pass the exam.

prompt: Broker Alan's neighbor, who holds no license, refers a buyer who later closes on a home through Alan's firm. Alan wants to pay the neighbor $500 from the commission as a thank-you. What does TRELA say?

options.text: Nothing prevents it, as long as the payment stays below $1,000
Nothing prevents it, provided the buyer is told in writing
The payment must be routed through the title company as a closing credit
A broker may not pay brokerage compensation to an unlicensed person

explanation: TRELA prohibits a license holder from paying a commission or fee to, or dividing a commission with, anyone who is not licensed for performing brokerage acts, including procuring prospects. A referral that leads to a sale is procuring a buyer, so paying the unlicensed neighbor violates the Act regardless of the amount or any disclosure.

distractorExplanations.a: TRELA sets no dollar safe harbor; any brokerage fee to an unlicensed person is prohibited.
distractorExplanations.b: Disclosure does not cure the violation; the problem is paying an unlicensed person for procuring a prospect.
distractorExplanations.c: Routing the money through closing changes nothing and could also raise RESPA kickback issues.

prompt: A Texas broker receives a buyer referral from a Colorado broker who has no Texas license and does no work in Texas. May the Texas broker pay the Colorado broker a referral fee?

options.text: No, because every fee recipient must hold a Texas license
Yes, if the Colorado broker conducts no negotiations in Texas
Yes, if the Colorado broker first obtains a temporary Texas license
No, unless the buyer pays the fee directly to the Colorado broker

explanation: TRELA lets a Texas broker share compensation with a broker licensed in another state, as long as the out-of-state broker does not conduct in Texas any of the negotiations for which the fee is paid. A pure referral qualifies. If the Colorado broker came to Texas to show or negotiate, a Texas license would be required.

distractorExplanations.a: TRELA has a specific exception for brokers licensed in another state who refer business without negotiating in Texas.
distractorExplanations.c: Texas does not issue temporary licenses for referrals; the out-of-state exception works without one.
distractorExplanations.d: Having the buyer pay directly does not change the rule and would bypass the brokers' own compensation agreement.

prompt: Three agents form an LLC that will act as a Texas real estate brokerage. What does TRELA require for the LLC to broker transactions?

options.text: Its own entity license, with a designated Texas broker as a manager
No separate license, since each owner holds a personal agent license
Its own entity license, with any sales agent named as supervisor
Registration with the Secretary of State in place of TREC licensing

explanation: A corporation, LLC, or similar entity that brokers real estate must hold its own TREC business entity license and designate an individual who holds an active Texas broker license and is an officer or manager to be responsible for its brokerage activity. If the designated broker owns less than 10% of the entity, TRELA also requires errors-and-omissions coverage.

distractorExplanations.b: Personal licenses do not authorize the entity itself to act as a broker; the LLC needs its own license.
distractorExplanations.c: The designated person must be a licensed Texas broker; a sales agent cannot be responsible for the entity's brokerage.
distractorExplanations.d: Forming the LLC with the Secretary of State creates the company but grants no right to engage in brokerage.

prompt: A Texas brokerage is launching a new website. Under TREC rules, what must its home page include?

options.text: The broker's commission schedule and recent closing prices
Scanned copies of every sponsored agent's license history
Links to TREC's IABS form and Consumer Protection Notice
The broker's errors-and-omissions policy number and limits

explanation: TREC rules require each broker and sponsored agent business website to provide, in a readily noticeable place on the home page, links labeled for the Texas Real Estate Commission Information About Brokerage Services and the Texas Real Estate Commission Consumer Protection Notice. Brokers must also display the Consumer Protection Notice at each place of business.

distractorExplanations.a: Commission schedules are not required, and posting them could raise antitrust concerns; the required items are the TREC notice links.
distractorExplanations.b: Agent license records are public on TREC's website, so brokerages need not post them; the required items are two notice links.
distractorExplanations.d: Insurance details are not a required website disclosure; TREC requires links to its consumer notices.

prompt: A sponsored sales agent misrepresents a home's square footage while working a listing for her brokerage. Under TRELA, who can be held responsible?

options.text: The agent by herself, since brokers are not liable for agents' acts
The seller by herself, since the agent spoke for the seller
The buyer, who should have measured the home before buying
The agent and her sponsoring broker, who supervises her acts

explanation: TRELA makes a broker responsible for the authorized acts of the sales agents the broker sponsors, and TREC rules require brokers to supervise those agents. The agent who made the misrepresentation is personally accountable, and the sponsoring broker can face discipline or civil liability for failing to supervise.

distractorExplanations.a: Brokers are responsible for the authorized acts of sponsored agents, so the agent does not carry the liability by herself.
distractorExplanations.b: The seller may face claims too, but the license holder's own misstatement exposes the agent and broker to discipline.
distractorExplanations.c: A buyer's chance to measure does not excuse a license holder's misrepresentation of a material fact.

prompt: During the option period, a buyer hires a home inspector. Which agency licenses Texas real estate inspectors?

options.text: The Texas Real Estate Commission
The Texas Department of Insurance
The Department of Licensing and Regulation
The Appraiser Licensing and Certification Board

explanation: Texas real estate inspectors are licensed and regulated by TREC, which also sets the required inspection report form and standards of practice. Appraisers are licensed by the Texas Appraiser Licensing and Certification Board, an agency administratively attached to TREC, while the Texas Department of Insurance regulates insurance and title rates.

distractorExplanations.b: TDI regulates insurance companies and promulgates title insurance rates; it does not license home inspectors.
distractorExplanations.c: TDLR licenses many trades, such as electricians and AC technicians, but real estate inspectors fall under TREC.
distractorExplanations.d: TALCB licenses and certifies appraisers; inspectors hold a separate TREC license.

prompt: Under current TREC rules, how long must a Texas broker keep trust account records and transaction files?

options.text: 2 years
4 years
7 years
10 years

explanation: TREC rules currently require brokers to keep trust account and transaction records for at least four years from the date of the transaction and to make them available to TREC on request. Longer retention can be wise for tax or litigation reasons, but four years is the regulatory minimum to know for the exam; confirm the current rule text.

distractorExplanations.a: Two years matches the license term, not the record-retention period, which is longer.
distractorExplanations.c: Seven years is a common tax-record habit, not the TREC minimum for brokerage records.
distractorExplanations.d: Ten years overstates the TREC minimum; brokers may keep files longer, but the rule does not require it.

prompt: An unlicensed friend helped a Texas owner find a buyer after the owner orally promised her 2% of the price. The owner now refuses to pay. Can the friend sue to collect?

options.text: Yes, because an oral promise to pay a finder's fee is enforceable
Yes, if two witnesses heard the owner make the promise
No, because she was unlicensed and had no signed writing
Yes, if she files the claim with TREC within one year

explanation: TRELA bars a person from suing to recover a commission for a real estate sale unless the person was licensed when the brokerage services began and the promise to pay is in writing and signed by the party to be charged. The friend fails both conditions, so she has no claim and may also have engaged in unlicensed activity.

distractorExplanations.a: TRELA requires a signed writing to sue for a real estate commission, so an oral promise is not enough.
distractorExplanations.b: Witnesses cannot replace the signed writing TRELA requires, and the friend is unlicensed in any case.
distractorExplanations.d: TREC does not decide commission claims, and no filing cures the lack of a license or a signed writing.

prompt: A bank asks sales agent Marco, through his broker, for a paid estimate of a foreclosed home's value to help set a listing price. What does Texas law allow?

options.text: Nothing, because only certified appraisers may estimate value for a fee
A full appraisal, as long as Marco signs as the appraiser of record
An estimate paid directly to Marco, bypassing his sponsoring broker
A broker price opinion, which may not be presented as an appraisal

explanation: TRELA allows license holders to prepare a broker price opinion or comparative market analysis for compensation, paid through the sponsoring broker. The opinion must not be called or used as an appraisal and must include the disclaimer language TREC requires. Appraisals are reserved for appraisers licensed or certified by TALCB.

distractorExplanations.a: Texas lets license holders give price opinions for a fee; certification is required for appraisals, not BPOs.
distractorExplanations.b: A license holder cannot sign as an appraiser; that requires a TALCB appraiser credential.
distractorExplanations.c: A sales agent may be paid through the sponsoring broker alone, so a direct payment would violate TRELA.

prompt: Sales agent Rosa missed her renewal deadline, and her license expired last week. A buyer client wants to see a listing tomorrow. What may Rosa do?

options.text: She may not show it until her license is renewed and active
She may show it, since TREC allows a 90-day working grace period
She may show it, as long as her broker comes along to supervise
She may show it, if the buyer signs a waiver of her license status

explanation: Brokerage activity requires a current, active license. Once Rosa's license expires, showing property or negotiating for compensation would be unlicensed activity, even if renewal is just a formality. TREC allows late renewal within set time limits for a higher fee, but she cannot practice until the license is active again.

distractorExplanations.b: A late-renewal window is a paperwork option, not permission to keep practicing while the license is expired.
distractorExplanations.c: Supervision does not substitute for a license; the agent herself must hold an active license to show property.
distractorExplanations.d: A consumer cannot waive Texas licensing requirements; licensing protects the public, not just one buyer.

prompt: Which description matches the membership of the Texas Real Estate Commission under current law?

options.text: Five members elected by licensed brokers in each region
Nine governor-appointed members: six brokers, three public
Twelve members chosen by the Texas REALTORS association
Seven legislators drawn from House and Senate committees

explanation: Under TRELA, TREC has nine members appointed by the governor with Senate confirmation: six licensed brokers with active practice experience and three public members who are not license holders. The public members bring consumer perspectives to the board, which adopts rules, promulgates contract forms, and oversees licensing and discipline.

distractorExplanations.a: Commissioners are appointed by the governor, not elected by license holders.
distractorExplanations.c: Texas REALTORS is a private trade association; it has no power to appoint state commissioners.
distractorExplanations.d: Legislators write the law but do not sit on TREC, which is an executive-branch agency.

prompt: When must a Texas license holder use a TREC-promulgated contract form for a client's transaction?

options.text: When TREC has a form for that transaction and no exception applies
When the brokerage has not adopted an in-house contract template
When no Texas REALTORS form covers the same transaction type
When the buyer is financing, since cash buyers may use any form

explanation: TREC rules require license holders to use promulgated forms when a form exists for the transaction. Narrow exceptions apply: a form required by a federal agency, a form prepared by an attorney and required by a property owner, or one prepared by an attorney for a principal. Brokerage templates and financing type do not change the duty.

distractorExplanations.b: In-house templates cannot replace a promulgated form; the duty to use TREC forms does not depend on brokerage choices.
distractorExplanations.c: Association forms fill gaps where TREC has no form; they cannot replace a TREC form required for that transaction.
distractorExplanations.d: The duty does not depend on financing; cash sales of resale homes also use the promulgated contract.

prompt: A buyer under the TREC One to Four Family Residential Contract paid a $300 option fee for a 7-day option period. On day 5 she simply changes her mind. What may she do?

options.text: Nothing, unless an inspection reveals a defect in the home
Terminate by giving the seller written notice before the deadline
Extend closing by 30 days, since that is what the option fee purchased
Terminate under the financing addendum and recover the option fee

explanation: The termination option paragraph gives the buyer an unrestricted right to terminate for any reason by delivering written notice within the option period (by 5:00 p.m. local time on the last day). The earnest money is refunded, but the seller keeps the option fee, which is credited to the price if the sale closes.

distractorExplanations.a: The termination option is unrestricted; the buyer need not cite an inspection defect or any reason.
distractorExplanations.c: The option fee buys a termination right, not a closing extension; extending closing needs a signed amendment.
distractorExplanations.d: The financing addendum covers loan denial, not a change of mind, and the option fee is not refunded on termination.

sourceNote: Original UniPrep2Go local bank (Wave 1). · Local QA repair (stems/distractors)

prompt: Which statement correctly describes earnest money under a Texas purchase contract?

options.text: It is the option fee under another name and is paid to the seller
It is the legal consideration without which the contract is unenforceable
It is a good-faith deposit; the mutual promises are the consideration
It is held by the listing broker in the brokerage operating account

explanation: A purchase contract is supported by the parties' exchange of promises, so earnest money is not what makes it binding. Earnest money is a good-faith deposit held by the escrow agent; it is applied to the buyer's costs at closing and can serve as liquidated damages or be refunded under the contract's terms.

distractorExplanations.a: The option fee and earnest money are separate payments with different purposes and recipients.
distractorExplanations.b: Mutual promises supply consideration; a contract can be valid even before earnest money is deposited.
distractorExplanations.d: Earnest money goes to the escrow agent named in the contract, never into a broker's operating account.

prompt: Buyer's agent Lena is completing the Special Provisions paragraph of a TREC contract. Which entry is appropriate there?

options.text: A warranty promising the seller will fix defects found within a year
New wording for the default paragraph that favors Lena's client
A list of known defects in place of the seller's disclosure notice
A factual business detail that no promulgated addendum covers

explanation: The form's own instruction limits Special Provisions to factual statements and business details applicable to the sale, and TREC rules bar license holders from using it for matters that a promulgated addendum covers. Writing warranties, remedies, or altered contract terms there is legal drafting, which license holders may not do.

distractorExplanations.a: A warranty with legal remedies is legal drafting, which license holders may not add in Special Provisions.
distractorExplanations.b: Rewriting form paragraphs is unauthorized legal drafting; Special Provisions holds factual business details.
distractorExplanations.c: Known defects belong in the seller's disclosure notice; Special Provisions cannot replace that statutory notice.

prompt: A seller signs a listing agreement naming Broker Kim as her agent. How was this agency relationship created?

options.text: Expressly, by an agreement that states the relationship
Impliedly, through the parties' conduct over time
By ratification of the broker's earlier unauthorized acts
By estoppel, because a third party relied on it

explanation: Express agency is created by an oral or written agreement in which the parties state the relationship, and a listing agreement is the most common example. Implied agency arises from conduct, ratification from approving acts after the fact, and estoppel from a principal's words or conduct that lead a third party to rely on an apparent agency.

distractorExplanations.b: Agency arising from conduct is implied agency, the opposite of an agreement that states the relationship.
distractorExplanations.c: Ratification approves acts already taken without authority; Kim's authority came from the signed listing.
distractorExplanations.d: Agency by estoppel protects a third party who relied on apparent authority; here the seller expressly hired Kim.

sourceNote: Original UniPrep2Go local bank (Wave 1). · Local short-stem expansion

prompt: Which list best describes the fiduciary duties a Texas broker owes to a client, as opposed to a customer?

options.text: Obedience, loyalty, disclosure, and confidentiality, owed to both parties
Obedience, loyalty, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting, and care
Honesty and fair dealing, the same duties owed to every party
Loyalty and confidentiality, without a duty to disclose material facts

explanation: A client is owed the full fiduciary duties often remembered as OLD CAR: obedience, loyalty, disclosure, confidentiality, accounting, and reasonable care. A customer (the other party) is owed honesty, fair dealing, and disclosure of known material defects, but not loyalty or confidentiality. TRELA also sets minimum duties for brokers who represent a party.

distractorExplanations.a: Fiduciary duties run to the client; the other party is a customer owed honesty and fair dealing, not loyalty.
distractorExplanations.c: Honesty and fair dealing are owed to every party; clients get the fuller fiduciary duties on top of them.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure of material facts is a core fiduciary duty, so a list without it misstates what clients are owed.

prompt: The seller of a Fort Worth resale home asks her listing agent to fill out the seller's disclosure notice for her. What is correct?

options.text: The notice is optional unless the buyer requests it in writing
The agent should complete it from her own walk-through notes
The seller completes it from her own knowledge, not the agent
The notice is required for pre-1978 homes as a lead disclosure

explanation: Texas Property Code section 5.008 requires most sellers of a single-dwelling residential property to give the buyer a notice disclosing their knowledge of the property's condition, with statutory exceptions such as foreclosure sales and certain estate transfers. It is the seller's statement, so an agent who fills it in risks liability; the agent may provide the form and explain it.

distractorExplanations.a: The statute requires the notice for most resale homes whether or not the buyer asks for it.
distractorExplanations.b: The notice reports the seller's knowledge; an agent completing it could become liable for its contents.
distractorExplanations.d: That confuses the seller's disclosure notice with the federal lead-based paint disclosure for pre-1978 housing.

prompt: After signing a TREC contract, buyer Sam transfers his right to buy the house to his sister, who will close in his place. What is this transfer called?

options.text: Novation, which replaces Sam under a new agreement
Recording, which gives public notice of the contract
Rescission, which unwinds the contract by mutual release
Assignment, which transfers Sam's contract rights

explanation: Assignment transfers a party's contract rights to another person, unless the contract restricts it. The assignor (Sam) generally stays liable if the assignee fails to perform. Novation, by contrast, substitutes a new party or obligation with everyone's consent and releases the original party.

distractorExplanations.a: Novation needs the seller's agreement to release Sam and substitute his sister; a simple transfer of rights is assignment.
distractorExplanations.b: Recording gives public notice of a document; it does not move contract rights to another person.
distractorExplanations.c: Rescission ends the contract and returns the parties to their starting positions; here the contract continues.

prompt: Buyer's agent Ana calls the listing agent to ask about a house for her client. When does TRELA require Ana to disclose that she represents the buyer?

options.text: At this first contact with the listing agent
When she submits an offer, in the contract's broker section
At first contact, if the listing agent asks whom she represents
Before closing, by noting it on the settlement statement

explanation: TRELA requires a license holder who represents a party to disclose that representation at the time of the first contact with another party to the transaction or that party's license holder. The disclosure may be oral or written. Ana's call to the listing agent is that first contact, so she must disclose before discussing her client's needs.

distractorExplanations.b: The broker information section confirms representation later; the statute requires disclosure at first contact.
distractorExplanations.c: The disclosure duty does not depend on being asked; it arises at first contact automatically.
distractorExplanations.d: Settlement-statement timing is far too late; representation must be disclosed at first contact.

prompt: Which arrangement is an example of a bilateral contract?

options.text: An open listing, where the seller pays a broker who produces a buyer
A purchase contract in which buyer and seller exchange promises
An option contract, where the optionor alone is bound to sell
A reward for a buyer referral, accepted by performing the act

explanation: A bilateral contract is formed by an exchange of promises, so both parties are bound from the start; a standard purchase contract is the classic example. In a unilateral contract one party promises and the other accepts by performing, as with open listings, option contracts, and reward offers.

distractorExplanations.a: An open listing is a classic unilateral contract: the seller promises payment, and the broker accepts by performing.
distractorExplanations.c: An option binds the optionor to sell while the optionee is free to walk away, which is the textbook unilateral example.
distractorExplanations.d: Acceptance by performance rather than a return promise is the definition of a unilateral contract.

sourceNote: Original UniPrep2Go local bank (Wave 1). · Local short-stem expansion

prompt: Seller Jo signs an exclusive right-to-sell listing with Broker Ray, then sells to a friend she found herself during the listing term. Is Ray entitled to the commission?

options.text: No, because seller-found buyers are excluded from this listing type
No, because Ray never showed the property to that buyer
Yes, because he earns the fee whoever finds the buyer in the term
Yes, but he must wait until the protection period after expiration

explanation: An exclusive right-to-sell listing entitles the broker to the agreed commission if the property sells during the term, no matter who procures the buyer, including the seller. An exclusive agency listing is the type that excuses the fee when the owner finds the buyer. The written listing's actual terms control.

distractorExplanations.a: Excluding seller-found buyers describes an exclusive agency listing, not an exclusive right-to-sell.
distractorExplanations.b: Showings are not the test; under this listing type the fee is earned when the sale occurs during the term.
distractorExplanations.d: The protection period extends the broker's rights after expiration; a sale during the term is already covered.

prompt: Broker Elena's firm lists a house and also represents a buyer who wants to offer on it. Both parties gave written consent to intermediary status. What may Elena do?

options.text: Personally advise both the buyer and the seller on what price to accept
Appoint one associate to advise both parties on price and terms
Act as an undisclosed dual agent without notifying either party
Appoint different associates who each advise one of the parties

explanation: TRELA lets a broker act as an intermediary only with both parties' written consent. The broker must act fairly and impartially and may appoint a different sponsored associate to each party, with written notice of the appointments. Each appointed associate may give opinions and advice to the party they work with; the broker herself may not advise either side.

distractorExplanations.a: An intermediary broker must stay impartial; advice to each party comes from separately appointed associates.
distractorExplanations.b: The same associate cannot be appointed to both parties; each party gets a different appointed license holder.
distractorExplanations.c: Texas replaced undisclosed dual agency with intermediary rules that require written consent and notice.

sourceNote: Original UniPrep2Go local bank (Wave 1). · Local short-stem expansion

prompt: A buyer signs a written buyer representation agreement with Broker Lee. What relationship does this create?

options.text: An agency relationship in which the buyer is the broker's client
A customer relationship in which the broker owes the buyer honesty alone
A subagency relationship in which the broker represents the seller
An intermediary relationship in which the broker serves both parties

explanation: A buyer representation agreement makes the buyer Broker Lee's client, so Lee owes the buyer fiduciary duties such as loyalty, confidentiality, and disclosure. The agreement also sets the term, the broker's compensation, and how it is paid. Intermediary status would require separate written consent from both parties.

distractorExplanations.b: A signed representation agreement makes the buyer a client owed fiduciary duties, not a customer owed honesty alone.
distractorExplanations.c: Subagency means working for the seller through the listing broker, the opposite of buyer representation.
distractorExplanations.d: Intermediary status needs written consent from both parties; a buyer agreement alone creates buyer agency.

sourceNote: Original UniPrep2Go local bank (Wave 1). · Local short-stem expansion

prompt: A buyer terminates during the option period and sends the escrow agent a written demand for the earnest money. The seller has not signed a release. Under the TREC One to Four Family contract's escrow paragraph, what may the escrow agent do?

options.text: Hold the funds until the closing date passes, then pay the seller
Notify the seller and release the funds if no objection arrives in time
Split the earnest money evenly between buyer and seller after 30 days
Move the funds to the listing broker's trust account until both parties agree

explanation: Under the current form, when one party makes a written demand, the escrow agent sends a copy to the other party; if no written objection arrives within the stated period (15 days in the current form), the escrow agent may disburse to the demanding party. A party who wrongfully refuses to sign a release can owe the liquidated damages and fees set out in the contract.

distractorExplanations.a: The escrow agent does not default to paying the seller; the form sets a demand-and-objection procedure.
distractorExplanations.c: Nothing in the form allows an automatic 50/50 split; release follows a signed release, a court order, or the demand procedure.
distractorExplanations.d: Moving funds to the listing broker is not an option; the named escrow agent keeps them until release.

prompt: Listing agent Rob tells a buyer that a Houston home has 'the best backyard on the street' and that the roof is 'two years old.' The roof is actually 14 years old, and Rob knew it. How are the two statements treated?

options.text: Both are puffing, since the buyer could inspect the roof
Both are misrepresentation, since neither is in writing
The backyard is puffing; the roof age is misrepresentation
The roof age is puffing; the backyard claim is misrepresentation

explanation: Puffing is an exaggerated opinion a reasonable buyer would not rely on as fact, such as 'best backyard.' A false statement of a verifiable fact, like roof age, that the agent knew was untrue is intentional misrepresentation. It can support license discipline and buyer claims even though the buyer could have ordered an inspection.

distractorExplanations.a: A buyer's chance to inspect does not turn a knowing false statement of fact into puffing; roof age is a verifiable fact.
distractorExplanations.b: Oral statements can be misrepresentation, and the backyard opinion is puffing whether spoken or written.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the test: subjective opinion ('best backyard') is puffing, while a false, checkable fact (roof age) is misrepresentation.

sourceNote: Original UniPrep2Go local bank (Wave 1). · Local short-stem expansion

prompt: A seller hands the buyer the seller's disclosure notice two days after both signed the purchase contract. What right does Texas law give the buyer?

options.text: To terminate for any reason within 7 days after receiving it
To terminate within 30 days if the notice reveals a material defect
To demand repairs of every item disclosed in the notice
To reduce the price by the cost of any defects disclosed

explanation: Under Texas Property Code section 5.008, if the seller's disclosure notice is delivered after the contract is signed, the buyer may terminate the contract for any reason within seven days after receiving the notice. That is why listing agents try to deliver the notice before an offer is made, so late delivery does not hand the buyer an exit.

distractorExplanations.b: The statutory window is seven days, and termination does not depend on the notice revealing a defect.
distractorExplanations.c: The statute gives a termination right, not a right to force repairs; repairs are negotiated between the parties.
distractorExplanations.d: Texas law does not create an automatic price reduction; the buyer's remedy for late delivery is termination.

prompt: A listing agent learns that the seller's elderly father died of natural causes in the home last year. The buyer has not asked about it. Under TRELA, must the agent disclose the death?

options.text: Yes, because any death on the property is a material fact to buyers
No, TRELA does not require disclosing a natural death of this kind
Yes, if the buyer's lender requires a stigmatized-property disclosure
No, because the seller has instructed the agent to keep it private

explanation: TRELA states that a license holder has no duty to inquire about or disclose a death on the property from natural causes, suicide, or an accident unrelated to the property's condition. The agent must still answer honestly if asked and must disclose known physical defects. Here the statute, not the seller's wishes, is why no disclosure is required.

distractorExplanations.a: TRELA specifically removes the duty to disclose natural deaths, suicides, or accidents unrelated to the property's condition.
distractorExplanations.c: Lender requirements do not create a TRELA disclosure duty for a natural death; the statute sets the rule.
distractorExplanations.d: The answer is no for a statutory reason; a seller's instruction alone could not excuse withholding a material defect.

prompt: Broker Sam is acting as an intermediary with no appointed associates. The seller privately tells him she would accept $20,000 below list. The buyer asks Sam whether the seller will take less. What may Sam disclose?

options.text: That the seller will accept $20,000 less, since he works for both
That the seller is flexible, as long as he gives no exact figure
Nothing about it unless the seller authorizes it in a separate writing
The figure, if the buyer first signs a confidentiality agreement

explanation: TRELA bars an intermediary from disclosing that the owner will accept less than the asking price, that the buyer will pay more than a written offer, or other confidential information, unless the party instructs otherwise in a separate writing. Hinting at flexibility leaks the same confidential fact, so Sam must decline to answer.

distractorExplanations.a: Working with both sides makes the intermediary neutral; it does not let him reveal one party's bottom line.
distractorExplanations.b: A hint that the seller is flexible still discloses confidential price information the statute protects.
distractorExplanations.d: The buyer's promise of confidentiality does not authorize disclosure; the seller's separate written instruction is required.

prompt: A broker's listing agreement says it lasts "until the property is sold" and states no end date. Why does this create a TRELA problem?

options.text: Texas listing terms are capped at a maximum of 90 days
Listings must be written on a TREC-promulgated listing form
Listings must let the seller cancel on 24 hours' notice
A listing must state a definite termination date

explanation: TRELA makes it a ground for discipline to fail to specify a definite termination date, not subject to prior notice, in a contract to perform services that require a license; property management contracts are treated differently. An open-ended "until sold" listing therefore violates the Act, whatever length the parties intended.

distractorExplanations.a: TRELA does not cap listing length; it requires a definite termination date, whatever the length.
distractorExplanations.b: TREC does not promulgate listing agreements; brokers commonly use association or brokerage forms.
distractorExplanations.c: No statute requires a 24-hour cancellation right; the requirement is a definite end date.

prompt: A buyer offers $310,000. The seller replies with a counteroffer at $318,000, which the buyer rejects. Can the seller now accept the original $310,000 offer and bind the buyer?

options.text: No, because the counteroffer terminated the original offer
Yes, because an offer stays open until the buyer withdraws it
Yes, if the seller accepts in writing within 24 hours
No, unless the original offer included an option fee

explanation: A counteroffer is a rejection of the original offer plus a new offer. Once the seller countered at $318,000, the $310,000 offer ended and cannot be accepted later. The seller can make a new offer at $310,000, but the buyer is free to accept or decline it.

distractorExplanations.b: A counteroffer ends the original offer by rejecting it; the buyer did not need to withdraw anything.
distractorExplanations.c: There is no 24-hour revival rule; a rejected offer cannot be accepted at any later time.
distractorExplanations.d: An option fee concerns a termination right after contract formation; it cannot revive a rejected offer.

prompt: A seller orally agrees on the phone to sell his house to a buyer for $250,000, then backs out. Why can the buyer generally not enforce the deal?

options.text: Oral agreements are void unless a notary witnesses them
The statute of frauds requires a signed writing for land sales
Sales above $100,000 must first be approved by TREC
The buyer did not deliver earnest money to the title company within three days

explanation: The Texas statute of frauds (Business and Commerce Code section 26.01) requires contracts for the sale of real estate, and leases longer than one year, to be in writing and signed by the person to be charged. An oral promise to sell land is generally unenforceable, which is why every purchase agreement is reduced to a signed contract.

distractorExplanations.a: Notarization is not what makes a sale contract enforceable; the requirement is a signed writing.
distractorExplanations.c: TREC does not approve private sales at any price; it regulates license holders and forms.
distractorExplanations.d: Earnest money timing matters under a written contract; here there is no written contract to enforce.

prompt: A 17-year-old who inherited a lot signs a contract to sell it. Before turning 18, he changes his mind. How is the contract treated?

options.text: Void from the start, so it never had any legal effect
Valid and fully enforceable against both parties
Enforceable against the minor once a parent signs later
Voidable, so the minor may choose to disaffirm it

explanation: A contract with a minor is generally voidable, not void: the minor may disaffirm it before reaching majority or within a reasonable time after, while the adult party stays bound if the minor chooses to perform. That is why license holders confirm every party's legal capacity, and why a minor's real estate is usually sold through a court-supervised guardianship.

distractorExplanations.a: A void contract has no legal effect for anyone; a minor's contract exists until the minor chooses to disaffirm it.
distractorExplanations.b: Lack of capacity gives the minor a right to cancel, so the contract is not fully enforceable against him.
distractorExplanations.c: A parent's later signature does not supply the minor's capacity; a minor's land is usually sold through a guardianship.

prompt: Under the TREC One to Four Family contract, the buyer fails to close without any contractual right to terminate. What remedies does the seller have under the default paragraph?

options.text: Keep the earnest money and also sue for all actual damages
Sue for damages, but the earnest money must be returned to the buyer first
Recover three times the earnest money as statutory damages
Enforce specific performance, or terminate and keep the earnest money

explanation: The current TREC One to Four Family form says that if the buyer defaults, the seller may either enforce specific performance and seek other relief provided by law, or terminate the contract and receive the earnest money as liquidated damages, releasing both parties. The seller chooses one path; keeping the earnest money ends the claim.

distractorExplanations.a: Taking the earnest money as liquidated damages releases both parties, so the seller cannot also sue for actual damages.
distractorExplanations.b: The earnest money is not automatically returned to a defaulting buyer; the seller may keep it as liquidated damages.
distractorExplanations.c: Triple damages relate to wrongful refusal to release earnest money, not to the seller's remedy for buyer default.

prompt: Under the TREC Third Party Financing Addendum, a buyer's lender denies her loan during the Buyer Approval period, and she delivers a termination notice on time. What happens to the earnest money?

options.text: It is refunded to the buyer
It goes to the seller as liquidated damages
It is split between the buyer and the seller
It is held until the original closing date

explanation: The Third Party Financing Addendum lets the buyer terminate by notice within the Buyer Approval period if she cannot obtain approval of the financing, and the earnest money is then refunded to her. If she misses that deadline, the contract is no longer subject to Buyer Approval, and a later termination for loan denial could put the earnest money at risk.

distractorExplanations.b: Liquidated damages apply when the buyer defaults; a timely termination under the addendum is not a default.
distractorExplanations.c: The addendum does not split earnest money; a proper termination returns it to the buyer.
distractorExplanations.d: Nothing in the addendum holds funds until the closing date; a valid termination triggers a refund.

prompt: Midway through a six-month listing, the seller dies before any buyer is found. What happens to the listing agreement?

options.text: It continues until the term ends, binding the estate
It terminates, because a principal's death ends the agency
It transfers to the seller's heirs automatically
It converts into an open listing for the estate

explanation: An agency relationship is personal, so it ends by operation of law when either the principal or the agent dies or becomes incapacitated. The broker must stop marketing and, if the estate wants to sell, obtain a new listing from the executor or administrator with authority to act.

distractorExplanations.a: Agency ends at the principal's death; the estate is not bound to the old listing without a new agreement.
distractorExplanations.c: Heirs do not inherit the listing contract; the estate's representative must sign a new listing.
distractorExplanations.d: There is no automatic conversion to another listing type; death simply ends the agency.

prompt: Listing agent Paula knows the home had foundation repairs and the walls are cracking again. The seller tells her not to mention it to buyers. What must Paula do?

options.text: Follow the seller's instruction, since she owes the seller obedience
Stay silent unless a buyer asks directly about the foundation
Disclose the known defect to buyers despite the instruction
Let the buyer's inspector find it, since buyers can inspect

explanation: TRELA makes it a ground for discipline to fail to disclose to a potential buyer a known latent structural defect or other known defect. The duty of obedience covers lawful instructions, so Paula must disclose. If the seller insists on concealment, she should explain the law and may withdraw, but she cannot help hide the defect.

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends to lawful instructions; concealing a known defect from buyers is not lawful.
distractorExplanations.b: The duty to disclose a known defect does not wait for a direct question from the buyer.
distractorExplanations.d: A buyer's ability to inspect does not relieve the agent of the duty to disclose a known defect.

prompt: A seller has already signed a contract with one buyer when a second buyer's agent sends listing agent Max a higher offer. What should Max do?

options.text: Reject it, because the property is already under contract
Hold it until the first contract fails, then present it
Forward it to the first buyer so they can match it
Present it to the seller, who may accept it as a backup

explanation: TRELA requires a broker who represents a party to present any offer to that party, and the duty does not stop once a contract is signed. The seller decides whether to accept a second offer as a back-up contract using TREC's back-up addendum, which takes effect if the first contract terminates. Max cannot decide on the seller's behalf.

distractorExplanations.a: The agent may not reject offers on the seller's behalf; the seller decides whether to entertain a backup.
distractorExplanations.b: Holding an offer withholds material information from the client; it must be presented promptly.
distractorExplanations.c: Sharing one buyer's offer with another buyer breaches duties to the seller and fairness to both buyers.

prompt: After the option period ends, the buyer and seller agree that the seller will replace the water heater before closing. How should they document the change?

options.text: On a TREC Amendment to Contract signed by both parties
In a text message exchanged between the two agents
By the listing agent initialing the original contract
On the seller's disclosure notice as an updated item

explanation: Changes to an executed TREC contract, such as repairs, price, or closing date, are made by a written amendment signed by all parties; TREC promulgates an Amendment to Contract form for this purpose. Agents' messages or initials are not the parties' agreement, and the seller's disclosure notice reports condition, not contract terms.

distractorExplanations.b: Messages between agents do not bind the parties; the change must be in a signed amendment.
distractorExplanations.c: An agent's initials cannot bind a party, and both parties must agree to modify the contract.
distractorExplanations.d: The disclosure notice describes condition; it does not change contract obligations such as repairs.

prompt: The seller needs to stay in the house for one week after closing and funding while her new home is finished. Which TREC form is designed for this?

options.text: Buyer's Temporary Residential Lease
Seller's Temporary Residential Lease
Addendum for Back-Up Contract
Notice of Buyer's Termination of Contract

explanation: TREC's Seller's Temporary Residential Lease covers a seller who stays in the property after closing and funding, setting rent, deposit, and duties. The Buyer's Temporary Residential Lease covers the opposite case, when a buyer moves in before closing. Without a written lease, possession passes to the buyer at closing and funding.

distractorExplanations.a: That lease covers a buyer who takes possession before closing, the reverse of this situation.
distractorExplanations.c: A back-up addendum sets up a second contract; it does not govern post-closing possession.
distractorExplanations.d: A termination notice ends the contract; this seller still wants to close and stay briefly afterward.

prompt: A buyer signs an offer on Monday with a 5-day option period. The seller counters on Tuesday, and the buyer accepts the counter on Wednesday, communicating acceptance that day. With no holidays involved, when does the option period end?

options.text: 5:00 p.m. local time on Saturday
5:00 p.m. local time on Sunday
5:00 p.m. local time on Monday
5:00 p.m. local time on the following Wednesday

explanation: The Effective Date is the date of final acceptance, here Wednesday, and the broker fills it in. Option days are calendar days counted after the Effective Date: Thursday 1, Friday 2, Saturday 3, Sunday 4, Monday 5. Under the current form the option period ends at 5:00 p.m. local time where the property is located on that fifth day.

distractorExplanations.a: Saturday counts five days from Monday, when the buyer signed the original offer, not from final acceptance.
distractorExplanations.b: Sunday counts from the seller's Tuesday counteroffer; the clock starts at final acceptance on Wednesday.
distractorExplanations.d: The following Wednesday counts business days; TREC option days are calendar days unless stated otherwise.

prompt: In a typical financed Texas home purchase, who conducts the closing and disburses the funds?

options.text: A title company acting as escrow and settlement agent
An attorney, because Texas bars title companies from closings
The listing broker, who prepares the settlement statement
The county clerk, who records the deed and forwards the wire

explanation: Most Texas residential closings are handled by a title company acting as escrow and settlement agent: it collects signatures, receives the lender's funds, records documents, pays off liens, and disburses proceeds. Some states use attorney closings, but Texas practice centers on title companies, with attorneys involved as needed.

distractorExplanations.b: Attorney-run closings are the custom in some other states; Texas closings are commonly handled by title companies.
distractorExplanations.c: Brokers do not act as settlement agents; the title company prepares statements and disburses funds.
distractorExplanations.d: The county clerk records documents but does not handle or disburse closing funds.

prompt: Three business days after a buyer receives her Closing Disclosure, the lender switches the loan from a fixed-rate to an adjustable-rate product. What does TRID require?

A corrected Closing Disclosure at the closing table, with no new wait
No new disclosure, since the buyer already received one
A new Loan Estimate, with closing allowed the same day

explanation: TRID requires a corrected Closing Disclosure when terms change, and three specific changes restart the three-business-day waiting period: the APR becomes inaccurate beyond tolerance, the loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added. distractorExplanations.b: Many corrections can be made at closing, but a product change is one of the three that restart the waiting period.

prompt: A buyer contracts to pay $250,000 for a home that appraises at $240,000 and takes a $216,000 loan. What loan-to-value ratio will the lender use?
explanation: Lenders base LTV on the lower of the sales price or the appraised value. Here the $240,000 appraisal is lower, so LTV = $216,000 / $240,000 = 90%. Dividing by the $250,000 price would understate the risk at 86.4%, which is why a low appraisal can force a buyer to add cash or renegotiate the price.

distractorExplanations.a: 80% is a common LTV benchmark, but this loan's actual ratio must be computed from the numbers given.
distractorExplanations.b: 86.4% divides the loan by the sales price; lenders use the lower appraised value.
distractorExplanations.d: 96% divides the appraisal by the price; that compares value to price, not loan to value.

prompt: A borrower earns $8,000 a month gross. Her proposed housing payment (PITI) is $2,000, and she pays $800 a month on a car loan and a student loan. What is her back-end debt-to-income ratio?
explanation: The back-end (total) debt-to-income ratio adds the housing payment to all other recurring monthly debts and divides by gross monthly income: ($2,000 + $800) / $8,000 = $2,800 / $8,000 = 35%. The front-end ratio uses housing alone: $2,000 / $8,000 = 25%. Maximum ratios vary by loan program and lender.

distractorExplanations.a: 10% counts the $800 of other debts by itself and leaves out the housing payment.
distractorExplanations.b: 25% is the front-end (housing) ratio; the back-end ratio adds the other monthly debts.
distractorExplanations.d: 45% does not follow from these figures; $2,800 divided by $8,000 is 35%.

prompt: A buyer takes a $200,000 fixed-rate, 30-year loan at 6% annual interest with monthly payments. How much of the first payment is interest?
explanation: Monthly interest = loan balance x annual rate / 12. Here $200,000 x 0.06 = $12,000 per year, and $12,000 / 12 = $1,000 for the first month. The rest of the roughly $1,199 principal-and-interest payment reduces principal, so each later payment carries slightly less interest as the balance falls.

distractorExplanations.a: $833 is one month's interest at 5%, not at the 6% note rate.
distractorExplanations.c: $1,199 is the full principal-and-interest payment; only part of it is interest.
distractorExplanations.d: $12,000 is the first year's interest, not a single month's.

prompt: A home sells for $400,000. The listing agreement pays the listing brokerage 3% of the price, and sales agent Kim's split with her broker is 70/30 in her favor. How much does Kim earn?
explanation: Listing brokerage fee = $400,000 x 0.03 = $12,000. Kim's 70% share = $12,000 x 0.70 = $8,400, and the broker keeps $3,600. Commission rates and splits are negotiable and TREC does not set them, so always compute from the agreement given in the problem.

distractorExplanations.a: $3,600 is the broker's 30% share, not Kim's 70%.
distractorExplanations.c: $12,000 is the whole listing-side fee before Kim's split with her broker.
distractorExplanations.d: $16,800 applies 70% to a 6% fee; the listing brokerage receives 3% here.

prompt: A seller's home sells for $300,000. She pays a total brokerage fee of 6%, has a $200,000 loan payoff, and pays $4,000 in other closing costs. What are her net proceeds?
explanation: Net proceeds = sales price minus all seller costs. Fee = $300,000 x 0.06 = $18,000. Net = $300,000 - $18,000 - $200,000 - $4,000 = $78,000. Forgetting any one deduction overstates what the seller walks away with at closing.

distractorExplanations.b: $82,000 leaves out the $4,000 of other closing costs.
distractorExplanations.c: $96,000 leaves out the $18,000 brokerage fee.
distractorExplanations.d: $100,000 deducts the loan payoff alone and ignores the fee and closing costs.

prompt: A title company offers a listing agent $250 for every buyer she steers to it for closing. How does federal law treat this arrangement?

options.text: Legal, if the fee stays under $500 per closing
Legal, if the agent reports the payment as income
A RESPA Section 8 kickback for a settlement referral
A TILA violation unless the APR is adjusted

explanation: RESPA Section 8 prohibits giving or accepting any fee, kickback, or thing of value for referring settlement service business, such as title insurance or closing services, on a federally related mortgage loan. A payment per referral is the classic violation, and neither disclosure nor tax reporting cures it.

distractorExplanations.a: RESPA sets no dollar safe harbor for referral fees; any thing of value for a referral is prohibited.
distractorExplanations.b: Tax reporting does not make an illegal referral fee legal.
distractorExplanations.d: TILA governs credit-cost disclosure; referral kickbacks fall under RESPA Section 8.

prompt: At closing, the lender sets up an escrow account for taxes and insurance. Under RESPA, what is the maximum cushion the lender may generally require in that account?

options.text: One month of escrow payments (1/12 of the annual total)
Two months of escrow payments (1/6 of the annual total)
Three months of escrow payments (1/4 of the annual total)
Six months of escrow payments (1/2 of the annual total)

explanation: RESPA's escrow rules (Regulation X) let a servicer hold a cushion of no more than one-sixth of the estimated annual escrow disbursements, roughly two months of payments, on top of the amounts needed to pay bills when due. distractorExplanations.a: One-twelfth is a single month; RESPA allows up to one-sixth, about two months.
distractorExplanations.c: One-quarter exceeds the RESPA cap, which limits the cushion to one-sixth of annual disbursements.
distractorExplanations.d: Half a year's payments would far exceed the one-sixth cushion RESPA permits.

prompt: An eligible veteran with full entitlement wants to buy a home in Dallas with no down payment. Which loan type is designed for this?

When the balance reaches 85% of the home's current appraised value
When the balance reaches 90% of the original purchase price

prompt: A Texas deed of trust securing a home loan names the borrower, the lender, and a trustee. What role does the trustee play?

Holds the power to sell the property if the borrower defaults
Guarantees repayment of the loan if the borrower cannot pay

prompt: A buyer closes on a Texas home in July and asks when the current year's property taxes will be due. What is the general Texas rule?

prompt: TxDOT needs a strip of a rancher's land to widen a highway, and the rancher refuses to sell. What must the state do to acquire it?

options.text: Obtain the rancher's written consent before it can proceed
Pay the land's appraisal district value for tax purposes
Rezone the strip for public use after a council hearing
Condemn it for public use and pay just compensation

explanation: Eminent domain lets government and certain authorized entities take private property through condemnation for a public use, even over the owner's objection, if they pay just compensation, generally fair market value. prompt: Which interest is a freehold estate rather than a leasehold?

options.text: A fee simple absolute held by a homeowner
An estate for years under a three-year office lease
A tenancy at will with no set end date
A month-to-month apartment rental

explanation: Freehold estates are ownership interests of uncertain duration, such as fee simple and life estates. Leasehold (nonfreehold) estates give possession without ownership: estates for years have a fixed term, periodic tenancies renew automatically (such as month to month), and tenancies at will last until either party ends them.

distractorExplanations.b: An estate for years is a lease with a fixed term, so it is a leasehold, not ownership.
distractorExplanations.c: A tenancy at will is possession by permission with no fixed term, a leasehold interest.
distractorExplanations.d: A month-to-month rental is a periodic tenancy, a type of leasehold.
